title: Particularity for fraud or mistake
summary: Rule 9(b) requires particular circumstances for allegations of fraud or mistake. The requirement concerns the pleaded theory, not simply the title of the statute under which the party sues.
notes: The full rule text (Rule 9) is in the supplement on file, PDF page 29, linked below. The casebook discussion does not make every consumer claim a fraud claim or replace the separate PSLRA requirements.

sections.Meaning: Rule 9(b) requires particular circumstances for allegations of fraud or mistake. The requirement concerns the pleaded theory, not simply the title of the statute under which the party sues.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify the allegedly false statement or omission, the responsible actor, relevant time and setting, and how it figures in the claim. Kearns examines consumer claims founded on a course of alleged fraud. Check the rule’s different treatment of mental conditions and any additional statute.
